$comment: Conversion surfaces. These are the reason the site exists. Every rule here is biased toward reliability over decoration — depth 0, no experiments, nothing clever.

cta-band.description: A full-width call to action between sections and before the footer. The one place in the library where depth is encouraged, because it should interrupt.

emergency.description: Restoration. Phone-first, high urgency, accent-heavy. The number is enormous and it is a tel: link.

children.notes: Carries the 24/7 / insurance-billing reassurance under the button.

appointment.description: Medical. Calm, dual-action: book online (primary) and call the office (secondary). Never urgent-sounding.

free-trial.description: Combat. The offer is the headline. Big, loud, unambiguous, zero friction between the visitor and the trial.
notes: Headline states the offer plainly — "Claim your free trial week", not "Begin your journey".

split-image.description: Copy one side, photograph the other. Calmer than the full-bleed variants and works well mid-page.

minimal-centered.description: One line and one button on a plain surface. For concierge and premium contexts where a loud CTA would undercut the positioning.

responsive.768: split-image stacks with copy first. Buttons become full-width. Padding steps down via the fluid scale.

a11y: Button text is specific — "Call now, 24/7" not "Click here".
Contrast measured against the scrim, never against variable media.
At depth > 0 the video is decoration only; the headline must be legible from the scrim alone.
invariants: Only one cta-band per viewport-height of scroll. Stacking two adjacent reads as desperate.

contact-block.description: The conversion surface. Where the lead is actually captured.

depth.description: ALWAYS 0. validate-config.mjs fails the build if a layout sets this higher.

form-map-split.description: Form one side, map and NAP the other. The default.

children.notes: Lazy-loaded, with a reserved aspect ratio. An eagerly-loaded map iframe is a classic CLS and LCP disaster.

form-only.description: Form on a plain surface, no map. Fastest, and correct where the business is not location-dependent.

multi-location.description: One card per location with its own map link, hours and phone. Group practices and multi-site restoration firms — often the most-used block on the whole site.

card-stack.description: Phone, email, address and hours as separate cards above the form. Scannable when someone wants to call rather than type.

responsive.768: Splits stack with the form first. The map moves below — nobody fills in a form after scrolling past a map on a phone.

a11y: Every input has a visible, associated <label>. Placeholder-only labelling is a failure.
Errors are announced via aria-live and linked to their field with aria-describedby.
The map iframe has a title, and the full address is available as text so the map is never the only source.
Phone and email are real tel:/mailto: links.
invariants: depth is 0. No exceptions — this is enforced in validate-config.mjs.
No depth-layer, no video, no canvas, no entrance animation on this section.
NAP here is byte-identical to the nav, the footer and the Google Business Profile.

lead-form.description: The form itself. Every field added costs conversions, so the default is short. Compliance constraints here are real, particularly in medical.

honeypot.description: Prefer a honeypot plus timing check over a CAPTCHA — CAPTCHAs cost real leads.

consent.description: Required where the niche or jurisdiction demands it.

short-3-field.description: Name, phone, and one free-text field. Restoration and gym trial signups. Highest completion rate of anything in the library.
notes: Field labels are niche-specific: "What happened?" for restoration, "Which class interests you?" for a gym.

standard.description: Name, email, phone, service select, message. The general-purpose form.

multi-step.description: Two or three steps with a progress indicator. Only worth it where the form is genuinely long — it trades a little friction for lower perceived effort.
notes: Each step is reachable and completable by keyboard, and progress is announced.
Never lose entered data when navigating back a step.

quote-request.description: Longer, qualifying form for commercial restoration and reconstruction, where a qualified lead is worth the added friction.

responsive.base: Inputs are at least 16px on mobile — anything smaller triggers iOS zoom-on-focus, which feels broken.

a11y: Visible <label> for every field. Placeholders are hints, never labels.
Required fields marked in text as well as with the required attribute.
Validation errors: announced with aria-live, associated via aria-describedby, and never colour-only.
Autocomplete attributes on name, tel, email.
Focus moves to the success or error message on submit.
invariants: MEDICAL: no PHI in a standard form. No symptom, condition, medication or history fields. Route anything clinical to a HIPAA-compliant intake or booking system. validate-client.mjs warns when neither is configured.
Submissions go to integrations.formRecipients and deliverability is tested before promotion — a silently broken form is the worst possible failure mode for these businesses.
COMBAT: link the liability waiver rather than embedding it. Do not collect a signature through this form.
